notes: Box score from the Spurs' 123–85 win over the Golden State Warriors on Nov 13, 2026 (NBA Cup, West Group C). The line score (38–25–34–26 to 14–19–27–25) is from Yahoo Sports and Sport Preferred and matches Field Level Media (38–14 after one, 63–33 at the half) and the AP (34–27 in the third; San Antonio won all four quarters). Spurs points, rebounds and assists are from the Bleacher Report box score; Castle's 12 of 18, 5 of 8 from three and 18 first-half points from Yahoo Sports and Field Level Media; Wembanyama's 12 points, 12 rebounds, 6 assists and 21 minutes from theScore and Field Level Media. The Spurs lines found this morning account for 96 of San Antonio's 123 points; the other 27 came from players not in Bleacher Report's list of top performers. Every Warriors point (85) is accounted for in the Yahoo Sports player ratings; LJ Cryer's 20 (7 of 17, 6 of 11 from three) is from Yahoo Sports, Bleacher Report and NBC Bay Area (Field Level Media has 19). Team totals (rebounds 60–43, paint 56–28, fast-break 21–3, 48 to 33 percent shooting) are from Yahoo Sports. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Friday's games.

San Antonio scored the first 18 points over the opening 4:29, eight of them by Castle, and Golden State missed its first 11 shots (Field Level Media); it was the biggest game-opening run of the play-by-play era (the NBA via ClutchPoints, Field Level Media). The lead reached 43 on a Harrison Barnes 3-pointer with 57 seconds left in the third (Field Level Media). Stephen Curry missed the game with an oblique tear (Field Level Media, Bleacher Report). The Spurs have won 11 straight after an 0–2 start (Field Level Media, San Antonio Express-News via Yahoo Sports) and are 2–0 in group play. They play at Utah on Sunday at 5:00 PM ET (AP).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Stephon Castle's 3-pointer with 10:08 left in the first quarter, off a pass from Victor Wembanyama, that made it 10–0 (SI.com live play-by-play; Castle's two threes and a jumper are the eight points Field Level Media credits him in the 18–0 run). The move isn't described further, so it is drawn as the template's plain pull-up. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the San Antonio Spurs or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Castle's listed 6-foot-6 and 215 pounds (RealGM), with arms scaled to the 6-foot-9 wingspan measured at the 2024 draft combine (Bleacher Report), in San Antonio's home white with No. 5 (RealGM). He has no approved look on file yet, so he is drawn as a team-colour silhouette in the kit. It is an original silhouette with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
